originalTitle: Australia news live: Chalmers says next election will be a ‘referendum on super’; new NSW laws to combat organised crime
content: How to get up to speed on the Australian political news of the day Today Guardian Australia launches a brand new political newsletter: Politics, really. No, really! We’ll be bringing you the latest political news – but more importantly, what it means. Sign up here. NSW police to ‘smash open’ online platforms where crime is plotted The NSW premier, Chris Minns, is holding a press conference about those organised crime laws. He says any “wilful and deliberate attempt to either evade law enforcement or use online platforms to facilitate crime, particularly murder, in NSW … will be a criminal offence”. Minns says criminal actors are basing themselves offshore and “pulling the strings” of people here using sophisticated technology. To combat that police will be given the latest technology themselves to “smash open and crack open online platforms to understand the full chronology of these criminal actions and their activities as they apply both here and overseas”. New laws being introduced in New South Wales aim to tackle organised crime by giving police more power and creating a new aggravated offence for conspiracy to commit gang-related murder. The maximum penalty will be increased to life imprisonment. Police would also be able to use new interim serious crime prevention orders to restrict people suspected of serious and organised crime. Those would be applied while the supreme court considers the full order. Children’s indictable offences would include activities linked to organised crime, and public shootings and firebombings would be added to the scheme. Police would also have more access to encrypted devices. The NSW premier, Chris Minns, said: Organised crime doesn’t stand still, and neither can the laws and powers we give police to fight it. We want to hit these criminal networks at every point – the people who organise the violence, the people who facilitate it online and the people who ultimately carry it out. If you conspire to arrange a gangland murder, you should face the prospect of spending the rest of your life behind bars. US access to Australian military bases This is an extraordinary story from Ben Doherty, Andy Ball and Nick Evershed about the extent of the United States’ access to military bases across Australia. Defence minister Richard Marles said in June that the “hugely significant American presence” in the region was a balance to China’s “very significant military buildup”. Read more: One Nation’s proposal for people to be able to divert some of their super into their pay packet is a “full-frontal attack” that will “make Australian workers tens of thousands of dollars worse off in retirement”, the treasurer, Jim Chalmers, said this morning. One Nation is “anti-worker” and they “vote the way that [billionaire backer] Gina Rinehart tells them to”, he said, adding that the next election will be a “referendum on super”: Every time One Nation is asked to support the financial interests of Australian workers, they oppose the financial interests of Australian workers. By ending super as we know it, by making Australian workers poorer as a consequence, One Nation is showing once again: this is exactly why One Nation poses an unacceptable and dangerous risk to Australian workers. Ryan to reintroduce lobbyist register bill Kooyong MP Monique Ryan will re-introduce her “clean up politics” bill to crack down on lobbyists and increase transparency. She argues gambling, tobacco, fossil fuel and mining representatives have too much access to politicians. Her bill would create a register for all lobbyists; stop ministers and senior public officials going straight from the government into the private sector; make ministerial diaries publicly available; and ban political donations for industries including gambling and tobacco. There are already plans to shake up the parliamentary pass system, while Ryan argues the government hasn’t done enough. Read more: Biggest urban solar farm in hemisphere set for Sydney’s ICC An 18,400 square metre solar farm that can generate 2.6GWh – enough to power up to 400 homes for a year – will be expanded across Sydney’s International Convention Centre (ICC). The state planning minister, Paul Scully, says it will be the biggest in any CBD in the southern hemisphere and will allow ICC Sydney to be 100% powered be renewables (through both the solar farm and through buying renewable energy): This is a great example of how we can unlock greater renewable energy generation and use in urban areas and power a vibrant city by taking advantage of building rooftops. Hosting the largest solar farm of any CBD in the southern hemisphere will help the ICC to reduce emissions and energy costs while also strengthening Sydney’s competitiveness in attracting major international conventions and events. One Nation super plan ‘no more than a headline’ Deputy opposition leader Jane Hume has some questions about One Nation’s proposal to divert superannuation contributions into people’s pockets. On ABC News Breakfast, she said: Well, this so far is nothing more than a headline. It hasn’t really been explained. Does the tax status of your superannuation, your discounted tax status, does that remain? Do you get a tax discount for paying your rent? How does it affect your concessional caps? How does it affect your bring–forward provisions, carry–back provisions? How does it affect your superannuation balance at the end of the day? Are we turning our superannuation funds into banks? None of these questions have been answered. Social media plans to give Australians ‘more choice’: Wells Labor will reveal draft rules that will give Australians “more choice” over what they see on their social media feeds, Anika Wells says. Speaking to ABC News Breakfast, the communications minister said the government’s draft digital duty of care bill will propose significant penalties for social media giants: We want them to observe the same basic safety standards, particularly for our children. chineseContent: 如何快速了解当天的澳大利亚政治新闻 今天，澳大利亚卫报推出了一份全新的政治时事通讯：政治，真的。不，真的！我们将为您带来最新的政治新闻 - 但更重要的是，它意味着什么。在这里注册。新南威尔士州警方将“捣毁”策划犯罪的在线平台 新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明斯 (Chris Minns) 正在就这些有组织犯罪法举行新闻发布会。他表示，在新南威尔士州，任何“故意和故意逃避执法或利用在线平台促进犯罪，特别是谋杀的企图……都将构成刑事犯罪”。明斯表示，犯罪分子正在海外建立基地，利用先进技术“操纵”这里的人们。为了打击这种情况，警方将获得最新的技术来“粉碎和破解在线平台，以了解这些犯罪行为及其活动的完整时间顺序，因为它们适用于国内外”。新南威尔士州出台的新法律旨在通过赋予警察更多权力并为串谋实施与帮派有关的谋杀设立新的加重罪来打击有组织犯罪。最高刑罚将增至终身监禁。警方还可以使用新的临时严重犯罪预防令来限制涉嫌严重和有组织犯罪的人。这些将在最高法院审议完整命令时适用。儿童可起诉的罪行将包括与有组织犯罪有关的活动，公共枪击和燃烧弹也将被添加到该计划中。警方还可以更多地访问加密设备。新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明斯 (Chris Minns) 表示：有组织犯罪不会停滞不前，我们赋予警方打击犯罪的法律和权力也不会停滞不前。我们想要打击这些危机
